All of this is in `src/tessel/views.py`. The `brain/` notes don't cover class-based views, so I read the source directly.

**Making the view function**
- You subclass `VerbView`, which extends `View`, and define `get()` and `post()`.
- `VerbView.__init_subclass__` runs at class creation. It scans the class for the names in `http_method_funcs` and sets `cls.methods = {"GET", "POST", ...}`. It also merges in any `methods` inherited from base classes.
- `View.to_view_func(name, *class_args, **class_kwargs)` is a classmethod that builds the plain function `view(**kwargs)`.
  - By default it creates a new instance per request, via `view.view_class(...)`. With `init_every_request = False` it shares one instance.
  - Either way, it calls `active_app.ensure_sync(self.run_view)(**kwargs)`.
  - It applies any `decorators`, then attaches `view_class`, `methods`, `provide_automatic_options`, `__name__`, `__doc__` and `__module__` to the function.
- You register it with `app.attach_route_rule(path, view_func=CounterAPI.to_view_func("counter"))`. The route picks up `view.methods`, so only those HTTP methods are allowed on the rule.

**Routing a method to the handler**
- `VerbView.run_view(**kwargs)` does `getattr(self, request.method.lower(), None)`, using the `request` proxy from `globals`.
- If the request is HEAD and there is no `head` method, it falls back to `get`.
- It asserts that a handler was found, then calls it through `active_app.ensure_sync(meth)(**kwargs)`, passing the URL variables.
